messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT - Dedicated pool 'lumen-enterprise-pool' GPU saturation detected. 8/8 GPUs at 100% and queue length 46. Pager: @Maya (oncall). Severity: SEV2. See /incidents/alerts/3456789012 for metrics snapshot.
Maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it — pulling dashboards and job list now.
Maya (oncall): top-level: backlog 46 requests, 92% of requests are generation streams, average queue wait 38s, tail latency spiking. Started ~2026-03-15T10:12Z.
Simon (eng-runtime): looking at runtime job table: most active is tenant 'lumen' running large batched generator jobs (job ids bg-1123, bg-1124, batch-9901). These are high-token fanouts.
Jen (SRE): any burst capacity left in us-west1? I see a regional burst token pool: available_nodes=4, max_burst_gpus=8 but tenant-level burst for lumen is disabled by policy.
Maya (oncall): checking tenant config: reserved=8 gpus, burst_allowed=false. Current queue > threshold for auto-burst but policy requires manual approve for enterprise tenants.
Nina (AM - Lumen): @Maya FYI Lumen is mid-day payroll processing window, they can't throttle externally. I can ping ops but they need us to minimize impact ASAP. :phone:
Oliver (CSM): I just joined the customer bridge with Lumen ops — they asked for a temporary lift of capacity for ~2 hours if we can. They prefer we do not drop requests.
Maya (oncall): proposed mitigations (short term): 1) enable temporary burst +2 GPUs immediately, 2) apply short rate-limit to non-priority routes, 3) route heavy batch jobs to 'batch-drain' queue with eviction policy, 4) fall back small requests to quantized model variant. Thoughts?
Simon (eng-runtime): +1 on burst. Also recommend routing small/low-context requests to int4 variant 'rwd-small-q' to reduce per-token GPU pressure. Expect ~25-40% token cost reduction; some quality regression.
Jen (SRE): operational steps to activate burst: run CLI ->
```
rbctl burst enable --tenant lumen --gpus 2 --ttl 120m --initiator maya
```
Also add an autoscaler override to prevent immediate eviction of other SLO-critical jobs.
Maya (oncall): running the command now.
Maya (oncall): command output: SUCCESS - burst allocation applied. New pool size: 10 GPUs (8 reserved + 2 burst). Scheduler informed.
IncidentBot: NOTE: Scheduler changes take ~25-40s to propagate. Watch metrics for queue drain.
Simon (eng-runtime): seeing queue drop: 46 -> 28 -> 14 over last 90s. GPU utilization down to 85%. Gradient of drain looks good.
Maya (oncall): applying per-tenant non-priority rate limit patch to reduce sudden load spikes:
```
PATCH /api/v1/tenants/lumen/config
{ "limits": { "non_priority_rps": 10 } }
```
Maya (oncall): patch applied — non-priority routes now capped.
Nina (AM - Lumen): Lumen ops confirms they paused two background batch jobs on their side, appreciating the assist.
Oliver (CSM): customer explicitly authorized the 2-hour burst window and confirmed they'll keep large internal batch jobs paused for at least 1 hour.
Jen (SRE): recommendation: monitor for 1 hour. If backlog remains >10 after 30m, escalate to infra to provision additional capacity or extend burst. Create follow-up ticket if we hit that.
Maya (oncall): handing off monitoring to Simon. I'll be available but switching to outcomes monitoring and cost notes.
Simon (eng-runtime): ack — taking watch. I'll set up a lightweight watch script to alert if queue increases by >10 within a 10m window and will notify infra.
OpsBot: Follow-up created: INC-3456789 | Owner: Simon (eng-runtime) | Severity: SEV2 | Actions: burst_enabled(2gpus, ttl=120m), rate_limit_applied(non_priority=10/s).
Maya (oncall): adding a mitigation note to the incident log: enabled tenant burst after customer approval; applied temporary rate limits; suggested model fallback for small requests. Cost impact estimated +$0.9/hr for 2 GPUs.
Simon (eng-runtime): queue currently 6, GPU util ~70%. I'll keep watch and escalate if it trends up.
Maya (oncall): thanks team. Oliver/Nina — please keep us updated if Lumen unpauses heavy batches.
Oliver (CSM): will do. Customer asked for a follow-up post-mortem to understand long-term capacity options (Reserved+Burst changes).
Maya (oncall): noted. Handing off page to Simon at 3456789120. Closing active remediation chat; will re-open on new alerts. :white_check_mark:
